The authors report within-subject contrasts (task blocks vs baseline/active control of meaningless images) and group-level voxelwise analyses (one-way ANOVA producing whole-brain t-maps and cluster-level activations). Participant age, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, baseline is active images rather than fixation-only, empirical data in healthy 18–60 y/o). Although sample size is small (n=8), this does not conflict with the stated inclusion/exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults investigating cognitive control processes (retrieval inhibition/interference resolution) using a within-subject part-list vs no part-list contrast and other within-subject contrasts (I5,I6). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with stereotactic coordinates and cluster-corrected statistics (I7,I8). The task assesses inhibition/interference—an executive function domain (I9). Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported (I10). No exclusion criteria apply: the study includes whole-brain results (not ROI-only), is not connectivity- or resting-state-only, reports within-group contrasts in healthy participants, and uses active task contrasts beyond fixation. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Excluded per E4: the study reports fMRI analyses but does not present a group-level whole-brain task-evoked activation map. It reports ROI-restricted activation analyses in the anterior cingulate and reports whole-brain psychophysiological interaction (functional connectivity) results, but no whole-brain task activation contrasts. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study using a task involving cognitive control/inhibition—emotional Stroop), I6 (within-participant contrast: positive vs neutral words), I9 (task falls within cognitive control/inhibition domain), I10 (participant age, healthy status, fMRI modality, and task described). Inclusion criterion not met: I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map reported). Therefore excluded under E4.

Full-text reviewed. Exclusion rationale: No exclusion criteria directly met. Inclusion criteria met: I6 (within-participant contrasts: duration vs control tasks), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/figures), I10 (healthy adult sample with ages reported and fMRI modality and task details). Inclusion criteria NOT met: I5 (study does not assess an established executive function or cognitive control task — it investigates duration/time perception), I9 (task does not fall within established executive function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, or initiation). Because the study’s task domain (temporal perception/duration discrimination) is outside the meta-analysis scope of executive function task activations, the study is excluded.

This is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (Go/NoGo), an executive function domain. The paper reports within-subject contrasts (Go/NoGo vs Go) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses for healthy controls and patients, with multiple-comparison correction and Talairach coordinates/tables/figures. Participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, within-group healthy activation maps are provided). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of Stroop interference (executive function/cognitive control) in healthy adults (mean age ~25.7). It reports within-subject contrasts of task conditions (RI vs CO, RI vs SI, SI vs CO, CO vs SU) and performs group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables of coordinates and figures. The task (size-Stroop) falls within inhibition/conflict domains of executive function. Participant demographics, imaging modality, methods, results, and discussion are fully reported in the provided full text. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, rest baseline only, non-empirical, or non-healthy/out-of-range ages) are met.

This is an fMRI study with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise maps and reported coordinates in healthy adults (meets I7, I8, I10). However, the task is voluntary breath holding (inhibition of respiration) rather than a standard executive-function task paradigm; the manuscript does not present a within-participant contrast of the executive/cognitive control task against an active control condition. Breath-hold events were modeled against resting/ongoing breathing and CO2 was included as a nuisance regressor rather than serving as an active control contrast. Therefore it fails I5 (clear task-based executive function paradigm), I6 (within-participant contrast vs an active control), and I9 (task clearly within established executive-function inhibition paradigms). It thus violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation or passive baseline used rather than an active control). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adults (n=16, ages 18–24) examining cognitive control/mindset implementation during an anagram task. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (each abstraction condition vs. the other two) and group-level voxelwise analyses with reported statistical parametric maps and coordinate foci. Whole-brain analysis procedures are described; results are reported as figures and tables of peak coordinates. Participant demographic and health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all reported. Although the authors used anatomically defined a priori ROIs for corrected inference in lateral PFC, whole-brain (gray-matter) thresholds and voxelwise group analyses were also performed and coordinates/figures are provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes children (6- and 10-year-olds) in addition to adults, so participants are not restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of an executive function — working memory CN-BT), I7 (group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported as coordinates/figures and clearly described), I9 (task falls within executive function domain — working memory), I10 (participant ages, healthy sample screening, imaging modality and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no clear within-participant contrast against an independent active control condition; the reported contrast is correct n-back responses vs. baseline/non-target trials, which does not fulfill the specified active-control requirement). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study uses a Stroop color-word interference task (an executive/inhibition task), reports within-subject incongruent vs congruent contrasts, provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/figures, and reports participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, and task details. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, it includes participants aged 47–72 yrs (range includes >60 years), which violates exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the 18–60 age range). No inclusion criteria are unmet. Because E8 is triggered, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis despite satisfying the other inclusion criteria.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=20, aged 22–30) including an n-back working memory task (an executive function). It includes within-participant contrasts (e.g., 1+2-back vs 0-back) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise activation maps thresholded at p=0.05 FWE (figures and cluster results reported). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are described. No exclusion criteria are met (whole-brain results present; not a connectivity-only or between-group-only study; active control used for n-back; healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, conclusions). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (n-back), an executive function, in healthy adults (11 male never-smokers, ages 20–40). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain (voxelwise) random-effects analyses (zero-order and first-order/parametric load effects) with voxelwise correction (P<0.05) and presents coordinates/tables and figures of activations. The task paradigm and imaging modality (fMRI) and participant demographics/health are clearly reported. Within-participant contrasts across working memory loads (parametric/first-order effects and load-specific 0/1/2/3-back vs rest maps) provide task-evoked activation maps suitable for meta-analysis of executive function. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; no exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-group-only, rest-only baseline, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy participants) are met.

This is an fMRI 2-back working memory study reporting whole-brain voxelwise results and within-subject contrasts (negative vs neutral; positive vs neutral). It provides participant age information, health status (healthy aged controls and aMCI patients), imaging modality, and task details. However, the sample comprises older adults (healthy aged participants) and patients with amnestic MCI, i.e. participants are outside the review’s target age range (18–60) and not restricted to healthy adults. Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E8 and cannot be included in a meta-analysis of executive-function activations in healthy adults aged 18–60. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: none. Exclusion criteria met: E8.

This is an fMRI, task-based study of cognitive control (flanker/ANT variant) reporting within-participant incongruent>congruent contrasts, random-effects whole-brain voxelwise analyses (with tables/figures/coordinates), and relevant participant age and task/modality details. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. However, the study sample includes a clinical group (high-functioning autism) in addition to neurotypical controls and is not restricted to healthy adults, which violates exclusion criterion E8. Although within-group whole-brain results for the healthy (neurotypical) participants are reported, the presence of non-healthy participants in the study leads to exclusion per E8. Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 were satisfied). Therefore the study is excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adult samples.

This is a task-based fMRI study of executive-related processes (sequencing/working memory/central executive) in healthy adults (n=18, age 19–36). It reports a within-participant cognitive subtraction contrast (REVERSE vs FORWARD) and group-level voxelwise SPM analyses with statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and cluster-level correction (p<0.01 voxel, cluster>7 voxels). Participant health, handedness, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group only, resting-state only, non-empirical, or out-of-range/clinical samples) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 18–50) using a task within an established executive-function domain (go/no-go inhibition). The paper reports within-participant contrasts (performed errors vs correct; observed errors vs correct; observed errors vs performed errors) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables/figures and coordinate reporting. Participant demographics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and is sufficient for screening.

This fMRI study investigates working memory (an executive function) with an event-related face WM task in healthy adults (ages 22–27). It reports within-participant contrasts (high vs low memory load; early vs late practice) and group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) mapwise analyses with thresholded maps and coordinate tables. Participant health status, age range, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. The high vs low load contrasts provide an active within-task control contrast of executive demand. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-groups only, and not resting-baseline-only), and the provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10.

This is an empirical fMRI study of verbal working memory (2-back) in healthy adults (ages 18–32), using a within-subjects design comparing auditory and visual working memory to matched active control tasks. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with corrected cluster thresholds and peak coordinates in tables and figures, and describes participant demographics and task paradigm. Tasks fall within the executive function domain (working memory). All required reporting elements (methods, results, discussion, tables/figures with coordinates) are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is a task-based fMRI study of spatial working memory (an executive function domain). It reports a within-participant contrast (CBT vs active baseline) at the encoding phase, with group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (FWE-corrected results reported and whole-brain activation tables/figures). Participant sample is healthy adults (n=19; mean age 26.1) and imaging modality and task paradigm are clearly described. All required reporting (methods, results, ROI and whole-brain analyses, behavioral data) is present and the full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (e.g., only ROI, connectivity-only, patient groups, rest-only baseline, or non-empirical paper) are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of healthy adults performing a 2-Back working memory task with an active 0-Back control, and it reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps and relevant participant information. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are satisfied. However, the sample age range is 20–62 years, which includes participants older than the allowed 18–60 range; this violates exclusion criterion E8. Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

The study is an fMRI investigation of working memory manipulation (executive function domain) in healthy adults and reports group-level, whole-brain task-evoked maps. However, the published fMRI contrasts are reported versus a fixation (rest) baseline: 'multisubject statistical maps for all tasks (color, angle, and dual) compared with fixation'. The meta-analysis requires at least one within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control condition (I6). Because the whole-brain reported maps use fixation as the baseline (a passive baseline) and no clearly described whole-brain task-versus-active-control contrast is provided, the study violates exclusion criterion E6. Inclusion criteria met: I5, I7, I8, I9, I10. Inclusion criterion not met: I6. Exclusion criterion met: E6. Therefore exclude.

This is an fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function domain) in healthy adults (mean age 22.8) using a task-based delayed serial recall paradigm. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (voxel-wise thresholds, cluster thresholds, stereotaxic coordinates, figures/tables). Crucially, it includes within-subject contrasts between task conditions (e.g., pooled ‘difficult’ vs ‘easy’ stimulus conditions; stimulus-condition ANOVAs and matched-samples t-tests), providing an active task-versus-task comparison rather than only fixation baseline. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text is incomplete (HTML skeleton only: title/metadata present; no introduction, methods, results, or discussion). Exclusion criteria met: none (unable to determine due to missing content). Inclusion criteria met: none. Inclusion criteria NOT met / cannot be confirmed: I5 (no information that this is an fMRI/PET task-based executive-function study), I6 (no within-participant contrast vs active control reported), I7/I8 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise results or coordinates reported), I9 (task domain not described/uncertain whether an established executive function task was used), I10 (no participant age/health status/imaging modality/task details reported). Because core article content is unavailable, I cannot verify required criteria; therefore exclude with low confidence and request full text for re-screening.

This study used task-based fMRI of working memory in unaffected first-degree relatives and healthy controls and provides group-level whole-brain maps and coordinate/figure reporting. However, the first-level and group contrasts are computed against an implicit baseline (rest) rather than an active control condition; thus it does not satisfy the requirement for a within-participant contrast versus an active control (I6) and meets exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation as the only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI working memory task), I7 (group-level whole-brain/voxelwise maps generated), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), I9 (working memory = executive function), I10 (participant age summary, healthy status screening, imaging modality and task described). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-subject contrast against an active control condition). Therefore the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (2-back) in healthy adults (N=18, age 28±7). It reports within-subject task contrasts (2-back vs a matched control condition with nonsense characters), performs group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 (figures and voxelwise maps described), and provides participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (4T fMRI), and task details. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis of executive-function task activations.

This is an fMRI study of passive viewing of violent, fearful, and neutral film clips in healthy adults. Although it reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked results (satisfying I7) and provides participant, health-status, and imaging details (satisfying I10), it does NOT assess an executive function or cognitive-control task (fails I5 and I9). The paradigm is passive viewing rather than an executive-domain task (e.g., inhibition, working memory, cognitive flexibility), and therefore there is no within-participant contrast of an executive function task vs an active control condition as required (fails I6). No exclusion criteria are specifically triggered. Full text appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Inclusion criteria met: I7, I10. Inclusion criteria not met: I5, I6, I9. Exclusion criteria met: none.

This is an fMRI, task-based emotion-word Stroop study with within-subject contrasts (unpleasant>neutral; pleasant>neutral), whole-brain voxelwise group analyses reported (tables/figures), and an executive-control/inhibition task paradigm. However, participant health status is not clearly restricted to or confirmed as a healthy sample: participants were recruited partly from an outpatient mental health clinic and the text does not explicitly state exclusion of psychiatric diagnoses or that the sample was screened to be clinically healthy. Because the meta-analysis requires samples restricted to healthy adults (Exclusion E8), I exclude this study despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This peer-reviewed article reports an empirical fMRI study using the stop-signal task (an established inhibition/executive control paradigm) in 33 healthy adult participants. The authors report within-subject contrasts (e.g., post-go speeding > post-go slowing) and present group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results (FWE-corrected maps, clusters, and coordinate tables). Participant demographics, healthy status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task methods are provided. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only contrasts, non-empirical, or out-of-range/unhealthy samples) are met.

This study includes both moderate-to-severe TBI patients and healthy controls and therefore is not restricted to healthy participants. Per exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals), it must be excluded from a meta-analysis of healthy adult executive-function task activations. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of executive function — working memory), I6 (within-participant contrast: mPASAT vs active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise random-effects analyses), I8 (coordinates and maps reported), I9 (working memory task — executive function domain), I10 (participant/sample, modality, and task information reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all I5–I10 satisfied). Full text appears complete.

The study is a task-based fMRI investigation of executive function (N-Back working memory) in healthy adults (ages 18–55). It includes within-subject contrasts of working-memory conditions (1-, 2-, 3-Back) versus an active control (0-Back sensorimotor), and reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with statistical maps and region findings (figures/cluster results, SVC applied to DLPFC). Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met: analyses are not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, and baseline is an active control task. Full text content (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore the study satisfies all required inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations in healthy adults.

Although the study provides suitable within-group, whole-brain fMRI activation contrasts for an executive function task in healthy adult controls (task-switch minus task-repeat) and reports necessary participant and task details, it includes a clinical sample (21 OCD patients) alongside healthy controls. Per exclusion criterion E8 (studies not restricted to healthy individuals), this study must be excluded from a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI), I6 (within-participant contrast in healthy controls), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables), I9 (task falls under cognitive flexibility), I10 (participant age/demographics, healthy-control status, imaging modality and paradigm reported). Inclusion criteria not met: none. Exclusion criteria applied: E8 (sample not restricted to healthy individuals). Full text appears complete.

This fMRI study uses an executive-function task (auditory verbal working memory) with an active control (vigilance QA) and reports within-subject contrasts (Q3A-INT vs QA). Group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise analyses are performed and results are reported for the whole sample and separately for control subjects (healthy adults), with coordinates and statistical thresholds provided. Relevant participant information (adult samples, screening/healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm) is reported in the full text. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; it appears complete. Although the study also includes a nonpsychotic relative group, the healthy control group provides qualifying within-group whole-brain activation maps suitable for inclusion in a meta-analysis of executive function activations in healthy adults.

This study must be excluded because it violates exclusion criterion E8: the sample includes participants outside the 18–60 years age range (subjects aged 7–57 years, i.e., children and adults). Although the study is of healthy participants, inclusion of minors prevents it from meeting the review’s age restriction. Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function via Stroop/inhibition), I6 (within-participant incongruent vs congruent contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses and maps), I8 (voxel-wise results reported in figures/tables), I9 (task is an established executive function domain—inhibition), I10 (reports participant ages, health screening, imaging modality, and task details). Inclusion criteria not met: none (all applicable I5–I10 were addressed). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion). Because E8 is met, the study must be excluded despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This is a methods/protocol paper (Nature Protocols) describing the emotional counting Stroop and expected fMRI effects; it does not present original group-level whole-brain, voxelwise task-activation maps or reported voxelwise results. The manuscript provides task design, anticipated results, and cites prior empirical studies, but no within-paper whole-brain analyses or statistical maps are reported. Therefore it meets exclusion E7 (methods-only/non-empirical paper). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task assessing cognitive control/interference) and I9 (task falls within executive function/inhibition domain). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant reported analysis results presented in this paper), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical map included), and I10 (insufficient reporting of participant demographics/healthy-sample details as original data in this paper). Conclusion: EXCLUDE due to E7; recommend consulting the cited empirical papers (e.g., Shin et al. 2001; Whalen et al. 1998) for potential eligible whole-brain results.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of attention and cognitive control using a dichotic listening paradigm. It reports within-subject contrasts (Attention × IID conditions) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise SPM analyses with FWE correction and cluster coordinates/figures. Participants are healthy adults (n=20, mean age 25.5). The task probes executive processes (top-down attention, conflict detection/resolution), and the paper provides participant, imaging modality, and paradigm details. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I5–I10 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This study used fMRI and task-based mental calculation but was conducted in 3 patients with intractable epilepsy (not healthy adults) and the main fMRI contrasts reported are mental calculation versus rest (passive baseline). There is no group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-activation map in a healthy sample. Therefore the study fails the review inclusion criteria requiring healthy adult within-participant contrasts against an active control and a group-level whole-brain map. Exclusion IDs met: E8 (participants are patients, not healthy adults) and E6 (rest/fixation was used as baseline rather than an active control). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (fMRI/PET study assessing cognitive control task) and I9 (task falls within executive function domain). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast vs active control), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise map), I10 (no healthy-sample confirmation/participants not healthy). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of response inhibition (stop signal task), an established executive function (inhibition). The study reports within-subject contrasts (successful vs failed stop trials) and performs group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and statistical thresholds reported. Participant details (40 healthy adults, ages 22–42, sex and handedness reported), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are all described. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, and participants are healthy and within 18–60).

This study is an fMRI cognitive task study (Stroop) in healthy adults and reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps, with participant demographics and task details. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (results reported in figures/tables), I9 (task within executive function domain: inhibition/ cognitive control), I10 (participant age, healthy status, imaging modality, paradigm reported). However, the study contrasts Stroop blocks against resting baseline rather than an active control condition; no within-participant contrast against an active control condition is presented. Therefore it fails I6. This triggers exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation only baseline without an active control). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Conclusion: EXCLUDE (fails I6; meets E6).

This is a task-based fMRI study of planning (Tower of London) in healthy adult participants (mean age 22.5; n=22). The paper reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., six- vs four-move problems; planning vs baseline), includes active control baseline conditions (visual and motor), and conducts group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM99) with cluster-level correction; results are reported as figures and coordinate tables. The task falls within the executive function domain (planning). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are all reported. No exclusion criteria were met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not rest-only baseline, empirical fMRI data in healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references, appendix).

This fMRI study uses a working-memory (executive) task, reports within-subject contrasts (categorical vs coordinate; task vs rest), and provides group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with coordinates/ROIs. However, the full text does not report participant ages (only N, sex, handedness, and healthy status). Inclusion criterion I10 requires reporting participant age along with confirmation of healthy sample, imaging modality, and task paradigm; the age information is missing. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered. Therefore the study must be excluded for not meeting I10 (participant age reporting).

Full text content provided is incomplete (only redirect/landing text) so core methods/results are not available. Based on available metadata: (a) Exclusion IDs met: none (unable to confirm). (b) Inclusion IDs met: I9 (task is spatial working memory, an executive function). (c) Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I5 (modality fMRI/PET not verifiable from provided content), I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control not verifiable), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise results not verifiable), I8 (reporting format of whole-brain results not verifiable), I10 (participant ages/healthy status/imaging and paradigm details not verifiable). Because the full text is incomplete, I cannot confirm that all inclusion criteria are satisfied and therefore exclude this record pending retrieval of the complete article (set fulltext_incomplete=true).

This study is excluded because it violates key exclusion criteria for the target meta-analysis. Exclusion IDs met: E6 (the task used rest/baseline fixation as the control condition rather than an active control) and E8 (participants are not restricted to healthy adults and age range reported includes older adults well above 18–60; sample includes MCI and AD patients as well as elderly controls aged 50–83). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI study of an executive function task — working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps reported), I8 (whole-brain results clearly described and displayed), I9 (task falls within executive function — working memory), I10 (participant age, health status of groups, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition — baseline was rest). Because E6 and E8 are fatal to eligibility for a meta-analysis restricted to healthy adults aged 18–60 with active-control within-participant contrasts, the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of working memory (verbal n-back), an established executive function domain. It reports within-subject contrasts (e.g., 2-back vs 1-back, 1-/2-back vs 0-back active control), and performs group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM with cluster- and voxel-level inference and reported coordinates/figures. Participant information (n=30, healthy right-handed adults, mean age 31±9, screened for health) and imaging modality (4 T BOLD fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of task-switching (cognitive flexibility), a recognized executive function. It reports within-subject contrasts (switch vs. repeat trials) comparing an executive condition to an active control (repeat trials). The paper includes group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (normalized beta-maps, voxelwise t-tests; reports a significant cluster in left superior parietal lobule with coordinates), and results are described in text and coordinates. The imaging modality (fMRI), task paradigm, and participant sample (nine undergraduate students) are reported; participants are adults and implicitly healthy. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not report only ROIs, connectivity, between-group contrasts only, resting baseline only, or non-empirical data, nor include non-healthy or out-of-range participants. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus it meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an event-related fMRI study of planning (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 18–32). The analysis uses a within-participant parametric modulation (ACT-R(t) regressor) and contrasts planning-load conditions (low/medium/high), providing a within-subject contrast of executive task-related cognitive processes relative to generic trial processes. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps are reported (t tests on the ACT-R coefficient) with activation coordinates and figures. The paper reports participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm, satisfying reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not resting baseline only, empirical with original human neuroimaging data, and participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for this meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

Full text is incomplete (only title/metadata provided). Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5 (fMRI modality is indicated by title/metadata), I9 (task concerns semantic/phonological maintenance — a working memory/executive task). Inclusion IDs not met/cannot be confirmed due to missing full text: I6 (cannot verify a within-participant contrast against an active control), I7 (cannot confirm group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results), I8 (cannot confirm reporting of whole-brain results in text/tables/figures), I10 (participant age/health and detailed sample information not reported). Because core methods/results are unavailable, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria; excluded and fulltext_incomplete=true.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (visual object and spatial delayed-recognition), which falls within executive function domains (I9). It reports within-participant contrasts comparing memory-delay conditions with active secondary-task conditions (e.g., Delay_location/no-distraction vs Delay_location/saccades; Delay_object/no-distraction vs Delay_object/passive listening), satisfying I6. The study used task-based fMRI (I5) and provides group-level whole-brain, voxelwise analyses with spatially normalized maps and tables of coordinates (I7,I8). Participant demographics and health status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported (healthy adults, ages ~22; I10). No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, include active control conditions, are empirical human neuroimaging with healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, figures/tables).

This is an event-related fMRI study of response inhibition (go/nogo), an executive function domain. It reports within-subject contrasts including direct comparisons between Movement Nogo and Count Nogo (task vs task active contrast), and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with thresholds and coordinate tables. Participant details (n=15, age 19–32, healthy), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Excluded for E8: participants fall partly outside the target adult age range (reported ages 16–21, including minors <18), violating the review’s 18–60 years restriction. Study otherwise meets the methodological inclusion criteria: I5 (task-based fMRI working memory), I6 (within-subject contrasts vs. 0-back active control), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster-thresholding and reported coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported with MNI coordinates), I9 (working memory = established executive function domain), and I10 (reports participant ages, healthy status screening, imaging modality, and task paradigm). No other exclusion criteria (E3–E7) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

The study is an fMRI, task-based investigation of working memory (n-back) in healthy young and older adults and reports whole-brain, voxelwise group analyses and within-participant contrasts between loads. Thus, it satisfies inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8 and I9. However, the provided full-text does not include numerical participant ages or age ranges (it refers to participant characteristics in Table 1, which is not included in the provided content). Inclusion criterion I10 requires relevant information about participant age; because age information cannot be confirmed from the provided text, I10 is not met. Additionally, the review exclusion criterion E8 (studies including participants outside the 18–60 range) cannot be assessed due to missing age data. Given that ALL inclusion criteria must be met and I10 is not satisfied in the provided material, the study must be excluded. No exclusion criteria (E3–E7) are directly violated based on the provided content.

Although this is a task-based fMRI study of inhibitory control (antisaccade) with whole-brain voxelwise group analyses and reported coordinates, it includes participants younger than 18 (adolescents 13–17) alongside adults and is not restricted to an 18–60-year-old healthy adult sample. This violates exclusion criterion E8 for the meta-analysis focused on healthy adults only. Additionally, the reported contrasts focus on reward vs neutral conditions within the antisaccade task and task epochs vs fixation baseline; the manuscript does not provide a within-participant contrast of the executive function (inhibition) task relative to an active non-inhibitory control condition required by inclusion criterion I6. Therefore, despite meeting I5, I7, I8, I9, and I10, the study must be excluded from this adult-focused meta-analysis.

Full text is incomplete: only title/metadata/redirect notice provided, so core methods/results are not available. From available information, I can confirm I5 (fMRI study assessing executive function) and I9 (task is inhibition, an executive domain). I cannot confirm I6 (within-participant task vs active control contrast), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps), I8 (reporting of whole-brain results), or I10 (reported participant ages/healthy status and full task details). No exclusion criteria can be confidently applied from the incomplete text (e.g., E4 plausible because this is an effective-connectivity study, but not certain). Therefore exclude due to incomplete full text preventing verification of required inclusion criteria. Exclusion IDs met: none. Inclusion IDs met: I5, I9. Inclusion IDs not met/uncertain: I6, I7, I8, I10.

This study meets multiple inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10): it is a task-based fMRI study of an executive function (working memory) n-back paradigm; includes within-participant contrasts (3-back vs 1-back); reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (with coordinates and thresholds); task falls within executive function; and participant/sample, imaging modality, and task details are reported. However, it must be excluded under E8 because the sample includes participants older than the allowed age range (older group aged 60–71), i.e., includes participants outside 18–60. No other exclusion criteria are met. Inclusion criteria not met: none.

This is an fMRI study using an n-back working-memory task (an established executive function) with healthy control participants. The paper reports within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 0-back) and group-level, voxelwise (SPM second-level) analyses for the control group, including whole-brain results and tables/coordinates and figures. Participant characteristics (healthy controls, matched for age/gender/education) and imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria for an executive-function task activation meta-analysis are satisfied, and no exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, only between-group contrasts, or inappropriate baseline) are met.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 20–40). It reports within-participant contrasts (distractor-plus vs control; correct vs error trials), uses group-level random-effects voxelwise analyses across the whole brain (SPM99), and reports activation peaks/coordinates in tables and figures. Participant/sample details, imaging modality, and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; not between-group patient comparisons; active control present; empirical with healthy adults). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

Exclusion met: E6 (study uses fixation as the only baseline/contrast). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI task-based study of executive function—antisaccade and ocular motor delayed response assessing inhibition and working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps were produced and used to define ROIs), I8 (results reported in figures/tables and described), I9 (tasks fall within executive function domains: inhibition, working memory), I10 (participant ages, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task details reported). Inclusion criterion NOT met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control task; the primary contrast is volitional saccade vs fixation). Because E6 is met, the study must be excluded from this meta-analysis despite meeting other inclusion criteria.

This study is excluded because it violates exclusion criteria E6 and E8. E6: the study uses fixation as the baseline (rest/fixation) alternating with ODR blocks and does not include an active control task contrast, so it relies on fixation as the only baseline. E8: the sample is not restricted to healthy adults (it includes a clinical schizophrenia group); although healthy control data are reported separately, the study population is not restricted to healthy individuals. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI of executive function - ODR), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with cluster correction), I8 (results reported via coordinates/figures/text), I9 (task falls within working memory/inhibition executive domains), and I10 (participant ages, healthy sample info, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast against an active control condition). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of executive functions (attention-switching and response inhibition) in healthy adults (aged 18–25) using task-based paradigms. It reports within-subject contrasts (switch vs nonswitch; incompatible vs compatible) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses thresholded with FDR, with peak coordinates and tables/figures described. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants are within 18–60 and screened healthy). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, I10) and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an event-related fMRI study in healthy adults (ages 19–31) using task-switching paradigms (response-switching and visual-switching) that probe cognitive flexibility/executive control. It reports within-participant, within-group voxelwise contrasts (switch vs stay) analyzed with random-effects, whole-brain statistical maps and thresholding, with peak coordinates provided in tables/figures. Participant characteristics, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigms are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants are within 18–60 and healthy). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis of executive function task activations.

This fMRI study used an executive function (Tower of London planning) task and reports within-participant contrasts (hard vs. easy problems) in addition to task vs. fixation. Group-level, whole-brain (SPM99) voxelwise results and coordinates are reported for both groups, and the paper provides participant ages, healthy control sample details, imaging modality, and task paradigm. Thus it meets criteria for an fMRI executive-task study with whole-brain group maps and an active within-task contrast. Full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is a task-based fMRI study (3T) that examines cognitive control processes (distractor inhibition/conflict monitoring) within a picture–word interference paradigm. The study reports within-participant contrasts between distractor types (e.g., categorical vs. unrelated/associative/phonological), uses whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (SPM5; FDR correction) with coordinates and tables, and provides participant demographics (healthy, ages 19–36), imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. The categorical-distractor contrasts specifically probe response inhibition/conflict monitoring and the authors discuss ACC and response-inhibition-related activations. No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), analyses are task-evoked (not resting-state or connectivity-only), and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Therefore the study meets the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and is suitable for inclusion.

This fMRI study examines cognitive control processes during cognitive reappraisal (task-based paradigm) and thus addresses executive/cognitive control. It reports within-participant contrasts (increase/decrease vs. look baseline) suitable as task vs. active control contrasts. Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses are reported (SPM group maps; tables of coordinates and figures provided). Reported results include coordinate tables and ROI-corrected amygdala analyses. The task engages established executive domains (inhibition/interference resolution, cognitive flexibility, working-memory-like maintenance/manipulation during reappraisal), and participant/sample details (N, mean age 20.6, healthy females), imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. Full text appears complete.

This fMRI+EEG study tests mental arithmetic (working memory/central executive) and reports whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results and coordinates, and provides participant age/health and task details. However the within-participant contrast compares mental arithmetic to an eye-closed resting baseline (passive rest) rather than an active control task. Therefore it does not meet the requirement for an active control within-participant contrast (Inclusion I6 not met) and meets Exclusion E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI assessing executive function), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps), I8 (whole-brain results reported as tables/figures), I9 (task within executive function domain — working memory/central executive), I10 (participant age/healthy status, imaging modality and paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (active control contrast). Exclusion applied: E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present). Consequently, exclude from meta-analysis per protocol.

This is an fMRI task study of cognitive control/executive function (temporal integration, working memory, strategy maintenance) in healthy adults (n=26, mean age 22.4). It reports within-subject contrasts between task conditions (W2 vs W12) and state/item decompositions, and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (cluster tables/coordinates, maps versus fixation and between-condition contrasts). Participant health status, age, imaging modality, and task details are reported. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of the Stop-signal task (inhibition = executive function) in healthy adult participants (N=126, all ages ≥18) reporting task-based, within-subject contrasts (e.g., StopInhibit–Go) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (thresholded/corrected; coordinates and figures provided). Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, not non-empirical, participants are healthy adults within 18–60). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This fMRI study reports task-evoked whole-brain activation during a verbal working memory (n-back) task in healthy adult controls, using an active control baseline (‘look for X’). It provides group-level voxelwise analyses (generic brain activation maps), regional coordinates/tables, and within-group contrasts (activation vs baseline) for the control group. Participant age ranges and healthy control status are reported, imaging modality and task paradigm are described. No exclusion criteria are met: the study does not provide only ROI/connectivity/between-group-only analyses, uses an active control baseline, and includes usable healthy adult whole-brain results. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Thus all inclusion criteria I5–I10 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Excluded because the sample includes participants outside the eligible age range (range 18–62 years), violating exclusion criterion E8. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI examining cognitive control/vigilance/working-memory updating in an oddball paradigm), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps reported for target-interval effects, with FWE correction and coordinates), I8 (whole-brain results reported and described in text/tables/figures), I9 (task falls within established executive domains: vigilance/working memory updating), and I10 (participant age range, healthy sample status, imaging modality, and task paradigm reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 — the paper does not explicitly report a within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition (e.g., target>standard); analyses focus on parametric modulation of target/novel responses by interval rather than an explicit task>active-control contrast. Full text appears complete.

This is a task-based fMRI study of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (n=16, ages 21–33). It includes within-subject contrasts (memory vs control; manipulable vs non-manipulable) and reports group-level, whole-brain, random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures. An active control task was used (digit comparison), not rest/fixation. Participant health, age range, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not between-group-only, and participants are healthy and within 18–60). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study satisfies all inclusion criteria I5–I10 and violates none of the exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of visual-spatial working memory (an established executive-function domain). It reports within-participant contrasts (task difficulty levels and conjunctions versus an active control condition where dots remained in the same position), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with FWE correction and tables/figures of coordinates. Participants were screened and described as healthy young and older volunteers; imaging modality (fMRI) and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, patient-only contrasts, or non-empirical) apply. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; whole-brain results are reported. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for executive-function task activations in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI task study of phonological working memory (working memory = established executive function domain) in healthy adults. It reports within-subject contrasts comparing working memory trials (pseudo-words) to an active control (digitally reversed speech), and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses using SPM2 with reported activations (tables/figures and coordinate reporting). Participant details (n=12, ages 22–39, healthy) and imaging modality and task paradigm are described. All inclusion criteria met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria are triggered: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity/rest-only, not a between-group-only comparison, uses an active control (not only rest/fixation), is empirical with original human neuroimaging data, and participants are healthy adults within 18–60. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore include.

This is an event-related fMRI study of working memory (an established executive function) with within-subject task contrasts (WM vs LTM and task phases) and group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported (maps, figures, and coordinate tables). Participants were healthy adults (ages 19–40), modality is fMRI, and task paradigms are clearly described. Although some contrasts are reported relative to fixation/ITI, the paper also reports direct WM vs LTM comparisons (within-participant), and whole-brain random-effects SPM results are provided. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical, task-based fMRI study of working memory and visual search in healthy adults (ages 19–32). It reports within-participant contrasts including dual-task vs an active control (‘Visual search only’) and other task contrasts, uses group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses with voxelwise statistical maps and reports coordinates/tables, and provides detailed participant, imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and task-paradigm information. The tasks fall within an executive function domain (working memory). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity/rest-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, out-of-range or unhealthy samples) are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) and none of the exclusion criteria.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for a meta-analysis of executive-function activations in healthy adults. It is a task-based fMRI study of response inhibition (Go–NoGo), an established executive function (I5, I9). It reports a within-subject contrast (correct NoGo vs correct Go) used in group-level analyses (I6). Whole-brain, voxelwise group results are presented and thresholded (SPM5; voxel-level and cluster-level FWE corrections), with coordinates and figures reported (I7, I8). Relevant participant and method details (demographics/age matching, confirmation of healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm) are provided (I10). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy subject maps). Therefore include the healthy-control within-group activation data for this meta-analysis.

This fMRI study used an N-back working-memory (executive) task with within-subject 2-back vs 0-back contrasts, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise activations (coordinates/figures), and provides participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task details (meets I5–I10). However, the sample includes patient groups (NPSLE and RA) alongside healthy controls and is not restricted to healthy individuals, which violates exclusion criterion E8. Although within-group contrasts for healthy participants are reported, the inclusion of non-healthy participants means the study does not satisfy the meta-analysis requirement to be restricted to healthy adults. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Decision: EXCLUDED due to E8.

Exclusion IDs met: E3 (study reports ROI-based regional glucose metabolism analyses with no whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps), E5 (no within-group whole-brain task activation contrast reported for healthy participants; analyses are correlational/ROI and between-group), and E8 (study includes patient sample and is not restricted to healthy individuals). Inclusion IDs met: I5 (PET study of executive function using Stroop task), I9 (task falls within executive function/inhibition domain), I10 (participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported). Inclusion IDs not met: I6 (no reported within-participant contrast of task vs active control at the imaging-analysis level), I7 (no group-level whole-brain voxelwise activation maps provided), I8 (no whole-brain results reported via coordinates/figures for voxelwise maps). Full text appears complete. Therefore the study must be excluded for this meta-analysis focused on whole-brain task activation maps in healthy adults.

This is an empirical fMRI study of task switching (executive function: cognitive flexibility/working memory integration) in healthy adults (mean age 23.6). It reports within-subject contrasts (transition cue vs task cue) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses with coordinates and figures (Z-thresholds and cluster criteria). Participant characteristics, imaging modality (3T fMRI), and task paradigm are fully described. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, not resting-baseline-only, not non-empirical, participants within 18–60 and healthy). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; fulltext is complete.

This is an fMRI task-based study in healthy adults (n=14, ages 19–31) that manipulated word-retrieval difficulty. It reports within-subject contrasts (word retrieval vs baseline; difficult > easy) and group-level random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (Pvoxel=0.001, cluster-corrected), with tables/figures/localizations. The task (verbal fluency/word generation) maps onto executive domains (initiation/controlled retrieval) and the authors specifically interpret right parietal activation as engagement of attention/executive control. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity-only; includes within-group contrasts; baseline is an active control; participants are healthy adults within 18–60).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of feature-based attentional control in healthy adults (mean age 24.3). The paradigm probes voluntary shifts of attention (cognitive control / cognitive flexibility) with within-subject contrasts comparing shift versus hold conditions. Analyses used a random-effects, whole-brain GLM with cluster-corrected voxelwise maps and reported Talairach coordinates and event-related timecourses. Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task details are reported. Thus all required inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, rest-only baselines, non-empirical design, or out-of-range/clinical participants). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is a task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function) that reports within-participant task contrasts (updating vs maintenance and task vs fixation) and presents group-level, whole-brain statistical maps (SPMs) and coordinate tables derived from multivariate CVA/NPAIRS. Participant details (ages, healthy control group characteristics), imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are reported. The study therefore meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10. No exclusion criteria apply: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity-only without task maps, include within-group healthy participant activations (not only between-group contrasts), and subjects are within the 18–60 range. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study examining cognitive control/attentional control over threat-related distractors (executive function domain). It reports within-participant contrasts (threat-related vs neutral distractor trials; block × trial interactions) and analyses modulated by state anxiety. Group-level voxelwise/random-effects analyses were conducted with whole-brain corrections and ROI small-volume corrections; coordinates and figures are reported. Participants are healthy adults (age 18–38) and imaging modality and task paradigm are fully described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

The study is an empirical, task-based fMRI investigation of cognitive control in healthy adults (n=21, mean age 33) using the Preparing to Overcome Prepotency (POP) task. It reports within-participant task contrasts (high-control vs low-control trials) and trial-by-trial analyses, and presents group-level voxelwise/task-related activations and whole-brain cluster results (figures/tables and supplementary tables). Participant demographics, health status, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary materials are referenced but not required for core eligibility. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text is not provided (only metadata/redirect page). Title indicates the study involves schizophrenia patients; cannot confirm a healthy adult within-participant whole-brain task activation contrast. Therefore it fails inclusion and likely violates exclusion E8. Inclusion criteria met: none could be confirmed. Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (uncertain if fMRI/PET and executive task in healthy adults), I6 (no evidence of within-participant contrast in healthy participants), I7/I8 (no whole-brain group-level maps provided in the available content), I9 (task domain cannot be confirmed as an accepted executive function in healthy adults), I10 (participant details and imaging modality not available). Exclusion criteria met: E8 (study involves/non-restricted to clinical population). Full text incomplete: true.

This is a PET study of the Stroop inhibition task with clear within-subject (incongruent vs congruent) contrasts, group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses, and healthy control within-group activation maps. However, the study recruited participants aged 18–70 (patients) and used age-matched controls, so the participant sample includes individuals older than 60. The meta-analysis exclusion criterion E8 excludes studies including participants outside the 18–60 age range (or not restricted to healthy individuals). Therefore the study must be excluded despite meeting the other inclusion criteria. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of cognitive flexibility (task-switching) in healthy young adults, reporting within-subject contrasts (e.g., bivalent > univalent; switch > repeat) and group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses (thresholded maps and tables/figures). Participant status (healthy, right-handed young adults), imaging modality (1.5T fMRI) and detailed task paradigm are described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore, all inclusion criteria are met (I5–I10) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that explicitly investigates top-down control/cognitive control during object categorization (manipulation of impoverished (MI) vs. less-impoverished (LI) stimuli). It includes within-subject contrasts (MI vs. LI) indexing increased executive/control demands, reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses with tables/figures, provides participant demographics (healthy young adults), and describes imaging modality and task paradigms. The behavioral Experiment 2 additionally manipulates working memory load, supporting the executive function interpretation. Therefore inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, I9, and I10 are met. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=14; ages 19–44) that explicitly investigates response inhibition, an established executive function domain. The study reports within-participant task contrasts (correct response inhibitions/lures versus target responses), and conducts group-level, whole-brain voxelwise one-sample t tests with cluster-level thresholding. Results are reported as stereotaxic coordinates (Table 1) and figures, and participant demographics, health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly described. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only analyses, no connectivity/rest-only analyses, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are healthy and within 18–60 yrs, and this is primary empirical data). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of working memory (executive function) in healthy adults with within-subject contrasts (high vs low memory load; reward vs low reward) and trial-stage contrasts (TARGET, DELAY, PROBE). Group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses are reported with coordinate tables and cluster-level correction. Participant age and health status, imaging modality (fMRI), and task paradigm are clearly reported. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This study is an fMRI/NIRS investigation of spatial working memory with whole-brain, voxelwise analyses and reports coordinates; it includes healthy adult control within-group results and provides participant and task details. Inclusion criteria met: I5 (fMRI of executive function - working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain maps), I8 (coordinates and figures reported), I9 (task is working memory, an executive function), I10 (participant, modality and task information reported). However, the study does not include an active control condition contrast; the task-related analyses use fixation/ITI or correct vs error trials and contrasts appear to be task vs baseline (fixation) or within-task performance contrasts rather than an executive task vs an active control task. The review exclusion criterion E6 (rest or fixation as the only baseline condition without an active control task) is therefore met. Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast of task relative to an active control) is not met. Because E6 is met and I6 is not satisfied, the study must be excluded from the meta-analysis.

Excluded because the study violates exclusion criteria: E6 (uses rest as the only baseline/contrast rather than an active control) and E8 (sample is not restricted to healthy adults — includes MS patients). Inclusion criteria met: I5 (task-based fMRI investigating executive-related functions — PASAT = working memory/sustained attention), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses reported with SPM and cluster thresholds), I8 (whole-brain results reported via figures/tables/coordinates), I9 (at least one task—PASAT—falls within an executive function domain: working memory/attention), I10 (participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported). Inclusion criteria not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of an executive task relative to an active control condition — baseline was rest/fixation). Because any exclusion criterion is sufficient for exclusion, the study should be excluded from the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI task study of visuospatial working memory (2-back) comparing users and controls. It reports a within-participant contrast (2-back minus match-to-center) and group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses with coordinates and figures. Participants are aged 19–21 and screened for Axis I disorders (healthy sample), and modality, task paradigm, and participant details are reported. The control condition is an active match-to-center task (not fixation). No exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI of an executive function (working memory n-back) including a healthy control group. It provides within-participant contrasts (2-back vs 0-back; 0-back vs baseline), group-level whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses for controls and patients, and tabulated MNI coordinates of activations. Participant ages, healthy control status, imaging modality (fMRI), and detailed task paradigm are reported. The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of a visual working memory (executive function) task in 20 healthy adults (mean age 39). The paper reports within-participant contrasts of task versus an active control condition (arrowhead task) and presents group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps (both univariate t-maps and SDM SVM maps) with results described in text, figures, and tables. Participant characteristics, imaging modality, and task paradigm are reported. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group patient comparisons, active control used, empirical data in healthy adults within 18–60). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria I5,I6,I7,I8,I9,I10 and should be included.

This is an fMRI study of speech motor control that examines preparation/initiation of syllable repetition (relevant to the executive subdomain 'initiation'). It reports group-level whole-brain voxelwise results (tables of MNI coordinates) and provides participant age/healthy-sample and task details. However, the study’s main within-subject contrasts compare task conditions to an implicit rest/ISI baseline (LCT > baseline; NCT > baseline). No active control task contrast (within-participant executive task vs active control) is reported as the primary whole-brain analyses. Thus it violates exclusion criterion E6 (rest/fixation-only baseline without an active control). Inclusion criterion I6 (within-participant contrast vs active control) is not met. Therefore the study must be excluded.

This is an event-related fMRI study of prosaccade vs antisaccade tasks (antisaccade involves inhibitory cognitive control). It reports within-subject contrasts (antisaccade vs prosaccade), group-level whole-brain voxelwise statistical maps with cluster correction and coordinates, and provides participant ages and healthy-sample status, imaging modality, and detailed task paradigm. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are met.

The study is an fMRI task-based investigation of working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults and reports within-subject contrasts (manipulation vs maintenance; what vs where) using group-level, whole-brain random-effects GLM maps (FDR-thresholded) and coordinate tables. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I5, I6, I7, I8, and I9. However, the provided full text does not report participant ages (only 'thirteen right-handed subjects' and normal vision), so it fails inclusion criterion I10 requiring relevant participant age information. No exclusion criteria (E3–E8) are triggered in the provided text. Because ALL inclusion criteria must be met, the study is excluded on the basis of missing participant age information in the provided full text.

This is a task-based fMRI study in healthy adults that examines auditory duration discrimination involving short-term storage and comparison (working memory). The study reports within-subject contrasts (discrimination vs identification) using whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses with corrected cluster- and voxelwise results and provides coordinates and figures. Participants (n=12) are healthy adults (ages 24–45). Imaging modality (1.5T fMRI), task paradigms, methods, and detailed results are reported in the full text. Therefore all inclusion criteria (I5–I10) are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study is an fMRI investigation of bilingual picture naming (L1 vs L2). Although whole-brain, group-level voxelwise results are reported and participant/sample/task details are provided, the paradigm is a language production task rather than a canonical executive-function paradigm. Inclusion criteria met: I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise maps reported), I8 (results clearly described with coordinates/figures), I10 (participant age/healthy status, imaging modality, and task reported). Key inclusion criteria not met: I5 (not primarily an executive-function or cognitive-control task by design), I6 (no within-participant contrast of a defined executive-function task vs an active control condition), I9 (task does not fall within established executive-function domains such as working memory, inhibition, cognitive flexibility, planning, vigilance, initiation). Exclusion criterion met: E6 (study uses passive viewing/fixation baseline and lacks an active control task for isolating executive processes). Full text appears complete.

This study must be excluded because it violates the age restriction for the meta-analysis and lacks the required active-control within-subject contrast. Exclusion criteria met: E8 (sample includes participants outside the 18–60 age range — older group mean age 70.3) and E6 (analyses use an implicit/rest baseline rather than an active control condition for the executive-task contrasts). Inclusion criteria satisfied: I5 (task-based fMRI including an executive-domain task: working memory), I7 (group-level whole-brain voxelwise analyses conducted with SPM and random-effects), I8 (whole-brain results reported as tables/coordinates/figures), I9 (tasks include established executive-domain WM and vigilance/attention), and I10 (participant ages, healthy status, imaging modality, and task paradigms are reported). Inclusion criterion not met: I6 (no within-participant contrast of the executive task relative to an active control condition — contrasts are versus implicit baseline/rest). Because E8 (and E6) are violated, the study is ineligible for inclusion in this meta-analysis.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study of verbal working memory (an executive function) in healthy adults (ages 24–46). It includes within-participant contrasts isolating manipulation versus maintenance (lag-1 digit span vs digit span; digit span vs simple number detection) and uses group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses with SPM96 (results reported in tables/figures and described in text).
